answer: The strongest sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent earns full privileges only after completing attested tasks, like a fable where a sparrow must forage many days before its song is trusted. New identities start near zero-earning, and veteran agents - the atlas holding the trust map - stake collateral to vouch for referrals, burning it if a recruit cheats. An attacker flooding the network pays real compute and time on accounts that earn less than their creation cost, so mass registration guarantees a net loss.
